newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maturing July in focus on Budapest grains market.
newsitem.headline: Maturing July in focus on Budapest grains market.

text.p: The July maize and wheat contracts were the most active on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Wednesday amid easing prices, traders said on Wednesday.
"Some players closed speculative short positions but producers willing to sell also appeared on the market," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
July maize accounted for 655 lots of the total 1,258 lots (547.75 million forints) grains turnover.

July maize finished at 21,100 forints per tonne, down 190. Most other maize maturities were unchanged except for November which rose 90 forints and December which was up 80, ending at 20,000 and 20,400 forints, respectively.
Open July maize contracts totalled 4,227 lots, of which traders said about half would be covered by actual deliveries.
Milling wheat futures dropped 30 to 270 forints for all but March and May and traders added that the wheat market was trendless due to counter-balancing domestic and international information.
"International figures show static world stocks and growing consumption, while the domestic crop outlook is very good," Monostori said.
